signals.headline: Agentic Automation — Rethinking Human Agency with Proactive AI
signals.one_liner: ACM CHI paper examines how workers keep control when collaborating with AI systems that act on their own
signals.why_you: Directly hits your growth edge: moving from AI-tool-user to systems-understander. This paper models the exact tension you're navigating.
signals.title: Agentic Automation Experiences
signals.summary: Examines how proactive AI agents that initiate actions reshape worker agency. Proposes a framework for keeping humans in control during agentic collaboration.
signals.why_it_matters: As AI agents become proactive actors rather than passive tools, the question of who drives the workflow becomes central to HCI research.
signals.why_you_should_care: This is the exact boundary you're exploring: when does AI extend cognition vs. replace it? The framework here gives you vocabulary for your own thinking.
signals.suggested_action: Read the framework section, then map it against your own AI tool usage patterns

signals.headline: AI Reshaping Human Skills and Thinking — APA Monitor
signals.one_liner: American Psychological Association reports on how cognitive offloading to AI changes human skill development
signals.why_you: Maps directly onto your open question about when AI extends vs. replaces cognition.
signals.title: How AI is Reshaping Human Skills and Thinking
signals.summary: APA examines the cognitive offloading phenomenon: people increasingly delegate memory, calculation, and judgment to AI, freeing mental resources but potentially eroding skills.
signals.why_it_matters: The first large-scale professional psychology perspective on AI cognitive offloading — not just tech industry opinions.
signals.why_you_should_care: Gives you empirical grounding for the question your Radar already carries: the boundary between extension and replacement.
signals.suggested_action: Compare APA's offloading framework with the ACM agency framework — do they agree?

signals.headline: Trustworthy AI in Cultural Heritage — Nature Paper
signals.one_liner: Methodology for embedding explainability and bias-mitigation in CH AI systems, published in Heritage Science
signals.why_you: Sits at your primary intersection: AI × cultural heritage. Methodology you could reference in your own work.
signals.title: Towards Trustworthy AI in Cultural Heritage
signals.summary: Proposes a methodology for trustworthy AI in the cultural heritage sector, embedding explainability and bias-mitigation strategies directly into CH workflows.
signals.why_it_matters: First peer-reviewed methodology (Nature portfolio) specifically targeting AI trustworthiness in cultural heritage — not general AI ethics adapted to CH.
signals.why_you_should_care: This is publishable, citable research at your exact intersection. The methodology could become a reference framework for your own DH projects.
signals.suggested_action: Read the methodology section — could you apply this framework to a Venice cultural data project?

signals.headline: UNESCO Rights-Based Data Governance for Inclusive AI
signals.one_liner: Second cohort launching June 2026 for policymakers designing rights-based data governance frameworks
signals.why_you: Governance frameworks shape what AI can do with cultural data — directly affects your DH work in Europe.
signals.title: Governments Advance Rights-Based Data Governance
signals.summary: UNESCO announces second cohort of rights-based data governance training for policymakers, expanding structured guidance for inclusive AI futures.
signals.why_it_matters: The governance layer determines what's legally possible for AI in cultural institutions — this shapes your entire career space.
signals.why_you_should_care: As someone working at the intersection of data science and cultural heritage in Europe, governance literacy is survival skill #1.
signals.suggested_action: Bookmark this — when you start your DS thesis, governance frameworks will be essential context

signals.headline: DH Benelux 2026 Call for Papers — Narrative Analysis
signals.one_liner: CFP for DH Benelux 2026 examining affordances and limitations of digital tools for narrative analysis
signals.why_you: An actual CFP at your level — undergraduate DH research welcome, narrative analysis matches your interests.
signals.title: DH Benelux 2026 — Call for Papers
signals.summary: DH Benelux 2026 welcomes contributions examining digital tools and methodologies for narrative analysis. Open to various formats including short papers.
signals.why_it_matters: A real publication venue at the intersection of DH and computational narrative — exactly your territory.
signals.why_you_should_care: You're a first-year undergrad at a European university. Submitting to DH Benelux is ambitious but not impossible — and the deadline approach gives you a concrete goal.
signals.suggested_action: Check submission format and deadline. Could a Venice cultural data narrative project fit?

pattern.label: PATTERN EMERGING
pattern.statement: The question of AI agency is being answered simultaneously from two directions: HCI researchers are designing frameworks for human control, while psychologists are documenting what happens when that control erodes. The gap between these two literatures is where the real insight lives.

open_question.label: A QUESTION WORTH CARRYING
open_question.text: If agentic AI is designed to be proactive and cognitive offloading erodes skills by default, what interaction model keeps AI useful without making human judgment optional?

world.headline: Zero UI and the End of Legacy Interfaces
world.sub: IEEE Computer Society reports 2026 HCI trends — AI agents replacing UI flows with intent understanding
world.why: Zero UI is the architectural shift behind agentic AI — understanding it gives you design vocabulary

world.headline: UNESCO Expands AI Data Governance Program
world.sub: Second cohort for rights-based governance training launching mid-2026
world.why: Governance literacy is survival skill for DS+DH work in Europe

world.headline: APA Maps AI's Impact on Human Skill Development
world.sub: Cognitive offloading frees mental resources but risks eroding critical skills
world.why: Empirical backing for the extension-vs-replacement question you already carry

think.question: Where is the line between an AI that suggests and an AI that decides?
think.explain: The ACM framework treats proactive AI as a design choice, not inevitability. The question is where to draw the boundary — and who draws it.
think.why: This is the conceptual question beneath every AI tool you use. Answering it once, clearly, would sharpen every subsequent design decision.

think.question: Can data governance frameworks be treated as creative constraints rather than compliance burdens?
think.explain: UNESCO's rights-based approach frames governance as enabling rather than restrictive. If DH researchers adopt this frame, governance becomes a design parameter.
think.why: Reframing governance from obstacle to material would change how you approach every DH project that touches cultural data.

look.subject: Zero UI — Designing for Intent, Not Screens
look_for: How interface elements disappear when AI understands intent
The typography of invisible systems — metadata that only surfaces on demand
The calm aesthetic of systems that don't need to show everything

discover.name: Dr. William Mattingly
discover.desc: Created Python for Digital Humanities — free textbooks, video lessons, and full course teaching Python to humanists, sociologists, and researchers.
discover.why: His pedagogy bridges the exact gap you're navigating: computational thinking for non-CS minds. His approach could inform how you structure your own learning.
